title: や, か (or), だけ & くらい
description: Incomplete lists with や, choices with か, limiting with だけ, and approximations with くらい/ぐらい (vs. ごろ).

points.title: や: and (among other things)
points.summary: Noun や noun lists a few examples from a larger group: 'A, B and so on'. Often paired with など.
points.body:
**や** joins nouns like と does, but it says the list is **incomplete**: these are just examples.
- 本**と**ペンがあります: there's a book and a pen (that's all).
- 本**や**ペンがあります: there are things like books and pens (and other stuff).

や is often followed by **など** at the end of the list: 本やペンなどがあります.

や only connects **nouns**. It can't join verbs or adjectives (for those, use the て-form or たり, the latter at N4).
examples: かばんの{中|なか}に{本|ほん}や{財布|さいふ}などがあります。
In my bag there are books, a wallet and so on.
{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{掃除|そうじ}や{洗濯|せんたく}をします。
On my days off I do things like cleaning and laundry.

points.title: か (1): or
points.summary: A か B = 'A or B', a choice between options. It often appears as AかBか.
points.body:
Placed **between nouns**, か means 'or': コーヒー**か**紅茶 (coffee or tea).

You'll also see it repeated after each option: 月曜日**か**火曜日**か**.

On its own, か at the end of a sentence makes a question (an easy point not covered here). With question words, か makes 'some-' words: なにか (something), だれか (someone), どこか (somewhere), いつか (sometime).

Don't mix up か (or) with と (and): コーヒーと紅茶を飲みます = I drink both. コーヒーか紅茶を飲みます = I drink one of the two.
examples: ペンか{鉛筆|えんぴつ}で{書|か}いてください。
Please write with a pen or a pencil.
{明日|あした}か{明後日|あさって}、{電話|でんわ}します。
I'll call tomorrow or the day after.
{何|なに}か{飲|の}みますか。
Will you drink something?

points.title: だけ: only, just
points.summary: だけ limits something to exactly this amount or thing. It works with positive or negative verbs (unlike しか).
points.body:
**だけ** follows nouns, numbers and verbs to say 'only / just this much':
- 水**だけ**飲みました (I only drank water).
- 一人**だけ**来ました (only one person came).
- 見る**だけ**です (I'm just looking).

Particles が and を usually disappear after だけ (水だけ飲む), while に, で, と stay: 友達に**だけ**話しました.

**だけ vs しか (N4):** しか always needs a **negative** verb: 水しか飲みません. だけ is neutral, while しか stresses that it's 'not enough'. A common mistake is しか with a positive verb.
examples: {朝|あさ}はコーヒーだけ{飲|の}みます。
In the morning I only drink coffee.
{日本語|にほんご}は{少|すこ}しだけ{話|はな}せます。
I can speak just a little Japanese.
{見|み}るだけです。
I'm just looking. (in a shop)

points.title: くらい / ぐらい: about, approximately
points.summary: Amount + くらい/ぐらい = 'about'. For points in time, ごろ is standard instead: 3時ごろ.
points.body:
**くらい** and **ぐらい** are interchangeable and mean 'about, roughly' after a **quantity**:
- 10分**くらい** (about 10 minutes), 千円**ぐらい** (about 1,000 yen), 三人**くらい** (about three people).

**くらい vs ごろ:**
- **ごろ** = around a **point** in time: 3時**ごろ** (around 3 o'clock), 5月**ごろ**.
- **くらい** = about an **amount** or duration: 3時間**くらい** (for about 3 hours).

Asking 'how much / how long?' you can say どのくらい or どれぐらい: 駅までどのくらいかかりますか.

くらい can also express extent ('so … that'), which is covered at higher levels.
examples: {駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}いて10{分|ぷん}くらいです。
It's about a 10-minute walk to the station.
{毎日|まいにち}2{時間|じかん}ぐらい{勉強|べんきょう}します。
I study for about two hours every day.
3{時|じ}ごろ{来|き}てください。
Please come around 3 o'clock.

questions.prompt: かばんの{中|なか}に{本|ほん}（　）ペンなどがあります。
questions.explanation: **や…など** lists examples from a larger set: 'books, pens and so on'.
notes: 本のペン would mean 'the book's pen'.
か = 'or' — but など lists things that are all there.
本もペンなど is ungrammatical. も means 'also' and doesn't make a list with など.
questions.translation: In the bag there are books, pens and so on.

questions.prompt: Which sentence says there are **other things too**?
options: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{本|ほん}もノートもあります。
{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{本|ほん}とノートがあります。
{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{本|ほん}やノートがあります。
{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{本|ほん}かノートがあります。
questions.explanation: **や** signals an incomplete list. Other things may be on the desk too.
notes: AもBも means 'both A and B' and stresses both, not that there are other things.
と gives a complete list: exactly a book and a notebook.
か means 'or', so either a book or a notebook is there.
questions.translation: There are a book, a notebook and so on on the desk.

questions.prompt: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{掃除|そうじ}（　）{洗濯|せんたく}などをします。
notes: だけ = 'only' — it doesn't link two nouns in a list.
が would make cleaning the subject.
掃除も洗濯など doesn't work. も doesn't build a list with など.
questions.translation: On days off, I do things like cleaning and laundry.

questions.prompt: {飲|の}み{物|もの}はコーヒー（　）{紅茶|こうちゃ}、どちらがいいですか。
notes: コーヒーの紅茶 means 'coffee's tea'.
や lists examples ('coffee, tea, etc.'). It doesn't present two options to choose between with どちら.
コーヒーも紅茶 doesn't offer a choice.
questions.translation: Would you prefer coffee or tea to drink?

questions.prompt: ペン（　）{鉛筆|えんぴつ}で{書|か}いてください。
questions.explanation: **か** = 'or'. Use one of the two to write.
notes: ペンも鉛筆で is ungrammatical. も would need to follow both nouns.
ペンだけ{鉛筆|えんぴつ}で isn't grammatical — だけ doesn't link two nouns.
ペンの鉛筆 means 'the pen's pencil'.
questions.translation: Please write with a pen or a pencil.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}（　）{明後日|あさって}、{電話|でんわ}します。
questions.explanation: One of the two days, so **か** ('or').
notes: も would need to follow both days (明日も明後日も), and it means 'both'.
や lists examples and doesn't fit two specific days.
明日の明後日 means 'tomorrow's day-after-tomorrow', which is nonsense.
questions.translation: I'll call you tomorrow or the day after.

questions.prompt: {朝|あさ}は{水|みず}（　）{飲|の}みました。
questions.explanation: **だけ** = 'only' and works with a positive verb.
notes: だけしか is emphatic, but it also needs a negative verb.
しかだけ isn't a valid combination.
しか needs a negative verb (水しか飲みませんでした). 飲みました is positive.
questions.translation: In the morning I only drank water.

questions.prompt: （Only one person came.）パーティーには{一人|ひとり}（　）{来|き}ませんでした。
questions.explanation: With a **negative** verb, 'only one person came' is **しか…ない**. しか is the N4 partner of だけ.
notes: 一人だけ来ませんでした means 'just one person didn't come', a different meaning.
一人が来ませんでした isn't natural with a number like this.
一人も来ませんでした means 'not a single person came'. That's grammatical, but it means nobody came, which isn't the intended meaning.
questions.translation: Only one person came to the party.

questions.prompt: （{店|みせ}で）すみません、{見|み}る（　）です。
notes: くらい means 'about', which makes no sense here.
ほど means 'extent' and doesn't fit.
しか needs a negative verb.
questions.translation: (In a shop) Sorry, I'm just looking.

questions.prompt: {駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}いて10{分|ぷん}（　）です。
questions.explanation: A duration (10 minutes) plus 'about' is **くらい**.
notes: ごろ is for points in time (3時ごろ), not durations.
10分まで would mean 'until 10 minutes'.
くらいに can't be followed by です here.
questions.translation: It's about a 10-minute walk to the station.

questions.prompt: {昨日|きのう}は3{時|じ}（　）{寝|ね}ました。
questions.explanation: For a **point in time**, 'around' is **ごろ**: 3時ごろ (around 3 o'clock).
notes: 3時だけ寝ました would mean 'slept only at 3'.
3時まで寝ました means 'slept until 3', a different meaning.
In standard Japanese, くらい goes with amounts and durations. 3時くらい is heard in speech, but ごろ is the correct choice for a time point.
questions.translation: I went to bed around 3 o'clock yesterday.

questions.prompt: {毎日|まいにち}どの（　）{勉強|べんきょう}しますか。—2{時間|じかん}ぐらいです。
questions.explanation: **どのくらい** asks 'how long / how much?'.
notes: どのまで isn't a word.
どのごろ isn't a word.
どのだけ isn't a word.
questions.translation: How long do you study every day? — About two hours.

questions.prompt: {日曜日|にちようび}は{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む（　）、{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ます。
questions.explanation: **か** can also join verb phrases: 'read a book **or** watch a movie'.
notes: と only joins nouns.
読むも isn't grammatical.
や only joins nouns, not verbs.
questions.translation: On Sundays I read a book or watch a movie.

questions.prompt: {何|なに}（　）{飲|の}みますか。—はい、お{茶|ちゃ}をください。
questions.explanation: **なにか** = something. The はい answer shows it's a yes/no question.
notes: 何が飲みますか isn't grammatical — the drinker isn't 'what'.
や lists nouns — 何や doesn't make a question.
何も needs a negative verb.
questions.translation: Will you have something to drink? — Yes, tea please.

questions.prompt: {日本語|にほんご}は{少|すこ}し（　）{話|はな}せます。
questions.explanation: **だけ** with a positive verb: 'just a little'.
notes: 少しも needs a negative ('not even a little').
しか needs a negative verb (少ししか話せません).
少しほど isn't natural.
questions.translation: I can speak just a little Japanese.
